answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with a slow-release trust anchor. New agents start with basalt-level standing: hard, heavy, and slow to move, earning weight only by completing verified work over time. A lantern mechanism then makes behavior public: each agent history is visible to peers, so a sybil swarm spinning up hundreds of fresh identities cannot fake the long, consistent record of a real participant. High-value privileges, like jade-tier access to scarce resources, unlock only after honest participation, making mass identity creation expensive and pointless.
